fib.s4_intro: A few reference notions, checked against the Fiber Optic Association (FOA) and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
fib.s4_l1: Single-mode fibre: core of about 9 µm, used with lasers at 1310 and 1550 nm. Multimode fibre: core of 50 or 62.5 µm, used at 850 and 1300 nm.
fib.s4_l2: ITU-T Recommendation G.652: single-mode fibre with zero dispersion around 1310 nm, also usable around 1550 nm. ITU-T Recommendation G.657: single-mode fibre less sensitive to bending, in particular for access networks and inside buildings.
fib.s4_l3: Optical loss budget: the FOA uses typical losses of about 0.3 dB per connector and 0.15 dB per single-mode fusion splice.
fib.s4_l4: Checking a link: inspecting and cleaning connectors with a microscope, measuring insertion loss with a light source and power meter, OTDR for long links with splices or for troubleshooting.

fib.q1: Do I need experience to start?
fib.q1_a: No: the beginner level is for people with no previous experience of optical fibre, in particular tradespeople and electricians.
fib.q2: Can I take only some of the modules?
fib.q2_a: Yes, that is the idea of the modular format: you choose the modules that are useful for your work and combine them as needed.
fib.q3: Does the course lead to a certification?
fib.q3_a: Wisy Safety does not present this course as an official certification. Professional certifications exist, such as the CFOT from the Fiber Optic Association: they are issued by those organisations, after their own exam. The document issued at the end of the course is specified on request.
fib.q4: What are the duration and the fee?
fib.q4_a: They depend on the level, modules and format chosen, and are provided on request. Contact the team or call +32 2 318 86 59.
